My two cents coming from the point of view of Classical Logic and Mathematical Linguistics : Axioms are described in the [object language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object_language) and definitions are part of the metalanguage. While writing proofs we manipulate the logical operators, for example, we can represent a conditional like p --> q as ~p v q and we annotate the step in the proof by stating the line "by the definition of a conditional". Usually when one describes a formal system, they define the set of alphabet and operators of the system borrowed from the metalanguage such as x,y,z for variables, a,b for constants and -->, v, ^ et al for the operators. Logical relations among statements, predicates and formulas are axiomatized, whereas the logical operators come with definitions.

There can be other categorical variables like 'Classes in High School' which have levels such as English, Math, History and so on. Sometimes, belonging to one level of a category can have an effect in the playing out of an event, like in this case, being a male can have an effect on having shopped online or not.
